intro: During training, BatchNorm observes the current batch. During inference, it must use saved statistics. Confusing these modes makes one example depend on unrelated inference inputs.
task: Return the normalized output and the next running statistics for a feature matrix. Make the training-to-inference state transition visible without mutating the caller’s arrays.
signature: batch_norm(x, gamma, beta, running_mean, running_var, training=True, momentum=0.1, eps=1e-5)
requirements: x is a nonempty (N,D) matrix. gamma, beta, running_mean and running_var have shape (D,); running_var is nonnegative. training must be a boolean, 0<=momentum<=1, and eps>0.
Training uses the feature-wise batch mean and population variance (divide by N). Both next running statistics equal (1-momentum)*old + momentum*batch statistic.
Inference uses the supplied running statistics and returns unchanged copies of them. In both modes output=gamma*(x-mean)/sqrt(var+eps)+beta.

Return a dictionary with output, running_mean and running_var arrays. This educational convention updates running variance with population variance; it is not PyTorch BatchNorm’s unbiased running-variance convention.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Training transition
examples.input: x=[[1],[3]], gamma=[1], beta=[0], running_mean=[0], running_var=[0], training=True, momentum=0.5, eps=3

hints.title: Reduce over examples
hints.body: Each column is one feature. Reduce axis zero, leaving a vector that broadcasts across rows.

hints.title: Keep the normalization and state update separate
hints.body: Training output uses current batch statistics, not the newly averaged running statistics.

explanation: Training output centers each feature before applying gamma and beta. Running state accumulates information across batches; momentum here is the weight assigned to the newest batch.
Inference output for an example is independent of other rows in its batch when the saved state is fixed. This distinction matters when batch composition changes.
Adapted the upstream population-variance convention. Replaced in-place running-state updates with returned arrays and documented its difference from PyTorch’s running variance estimator.
